from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A ray rotates clockwise around an anchor.", "The ray encounters a point in space.", "The anchor switches to the new point."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of a Rotating Ray", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        anchor = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(anchor, 'C3')
        ray = Line(start=anchor.get_center(), end=anchor.get_center() + RIGHT * 2, color=WHITE)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(point, 'B5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(anchor), Create(ray))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Rotating(ray, radians=-PI/4, about_point=anchor.get_center()))
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        new_ray = Line(start=point.get_center(), end=point.get_center() + UP * 2, color=WHITE)
        self.play(FadeOut(ray), FadeIn(new_ray))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The line rotates continuously clockwise.", "It hits two points simultaneously.", "The pivot switches to continue rotation."]
        self.setup_layout("Core Mechanism: Angles and Pivot Switching", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Elements ---
        # Draw two intersecting lines
        line1 = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE).scale(1.5)
        line2 = Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).scale(1.5)
        axes = VGroup(line1, line2)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Angle arc
        angle = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/4, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(angle, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Pivot point
        pivot = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(pivot, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), FadeIn(angle), FadeIn(pivot))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Rotate(axes, angle=-PI/4, about_point=axes.get_center(), run_time=2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Indicate(axes))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        new_pivot = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(new_pivot, 'D4', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(new_pivot), axes.animate.move_to(new_pivot.get_center()))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Theorem & Result: The Periodicity", [
            "The windmill process is periodic.",
            "It completes cycles of finite rotations.",
            "Total turns relate to point permutations."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        blade = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        pivot = Dot(ORIGIN, color=RED)
        
        # Group for rotation
        windmill_group = VGroup(blade, pivot)
        self.place_at_grid(windmill_group, 'C3')
        self.add(circle, windmill_group)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(Rotate(blade, angle=PI, about_point=self.grid['C3']), run_time=3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=0.5)
        # Indicate cycle completion
        cycle_highlight = Arc(radius=1.6, start_angle=0, angle=2*PI, color="#00FFFF")
        self.add(cycle_highlight)
        self.play(Create(cycle_highlight), run_time=2)
        self.play(FadeOut(cycle_highlight))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=0.5)
        # Show periodic function sketch
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2*PI*x) + 1, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(axes, graph), 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["This concept aids convex hull algorithms.", "Geometry patterns reveal hidden structures.", "The windmill maps the entire plane."]
        self.setup_layout("Application and Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        vacuum = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.5, color=YELLOW)
        pivot = Dot(color=RED)
        arm = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, color=BLUE)
        windmill = VGroup(vacuum, pivot, arm)
        self.place_at_grid(windmill, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Rotate(windmill, angle=PI/2, about_point=self.grid['C3']))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        text_summary = Text("Structure: predictable patterns", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(text_summary, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(text_summary))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(FadeOut(windmill), FadeOut(text_summary), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title))

outline.topic: The Windmill Problem (Geometric Rotation & Convex Hulls)
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in competitive mathematics or geometry

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of a Rotating Ray
sections.content: Introduce the idea of a ray anchored at a point that rotates continuously. Explain that as the ray hits points in a 2D plane, it 'switches' its anchor point whenever it encounters a new point, maintaining a clockwise motion.
sections.example: Imagine a flashlight beam rotating clockwise in a field of fireflies; every time the beam hits a new firefly, that firefly becomes the new pivot point for the beam.

sections.title: Problem Definition: The Windmill Motion
sections.content: Define the Windmill process: Given n points in a plane, a line rotates around a pivot point (one of the n points). When the line hits another point, that point becomes the new pivot. Visualize this as a 'geometric dance' where the line is the windmill blade.
sections.example: Visualizing 5 points as stars in the sky. The 'blade' starts at Star A, sweeps until it hits Star B, then pivots to Star B to sweep for Star C.

sections.title: Core Mechanism: Angles and Pivot Switching
sections.content: Explain the logic of switching: The line rotates until it is collinear with two points. The 'next' pivot is the point that preserves the clockwise rotational direction. This is a greedy algorithm approach.
sections.example: An animation showing a clock hand. When it hits a point, the hand 'snaps' its center to that point and continues the sweep, ensuring the line never rotates counter-clockwise.

sections.title: Theorem & Result: The Periodicity
sections.content: Present the key knowledge point: The windmill process is periodic. For n points, the line will return to its original state after a finite number of rotations. Emphasize that the total number of turns is related to the permutation of points.
sections.example: A diagram showing the line completing a full 180-degree sweep cycle, demonstrating that the 'blade' effectively explores all possible line orientations defined by the set of points.

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
sections.content: Briefly mention that this process is used in computer science for calculating convex hulls and point-set triangulation. Summarize how geometry turns into predictable patterns.
sections.example: A 'Robot Vacuum' analogy: The vacuum (windmill blade) scans the room by pivoting on furniture legs to map the entire floor efficiently.
